intro.title: List Virtualization
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a scrollable list of items that uses virtualization to render only the visible items on the screen, dramatically improving performance for long lists. You will learn the core concept of list virtualization, which involves calculating and displaying only the portion of data the user can see, while keeping the scrollbar's size accurate. The main technologies involved are React for the UI, TypeScript for type safety, and a custom hook to manage the viewport calculations. By the end, you'll understand how to efficiently handle large datasets in a React application.
intro.usecase: List virtualization is essential for performance in real-world applications that display large datasets. You'll see this pattern in social media feeds like Facebook or Twitter, where only visible posts are rendered as you scroll. E-commerce sites like Amazon use it for product listings with thousands of items, and data dashboards implement it for tables with massive datasets. As a developer, you'll apply virtualization whenever rendering all items at once would cause noticeable lag or memory issues.
